candidates.name: BrowserArena
candidates.description: LLM-agent browser benchmark using dynamically generated live-web tasks specifically to resist contamination.
candidates.why_distinct: 2025-era, explicitly contamination-resistant design.

candidates.name: PokeAgent Challenge
candidates.description: Two tracks: competitive Pokemon battling (partial-observability opponent modeling) + RPG speedrunning (long-horizon agent orchestration). NeurIPS 2025 competition, ongoing.
candidates.why_distinct: Nothing in the catalog covers Pokemon-style long-horizon RPG play.

candidates.name: TextArena
candidates.description: 57+ competitive text-game environments (negotiation, deception, theory-of-mind); live public TrueSkill leaderboard, models play humans and each other.
candidates.why_distinct: Broader and live-ranked vs. Balrog's fixed NetHack focus.

candidates.name: UK AISI Inspect Evals / Inspect Cyber
candidates.description: Open-source eval framework + canonical eval packages (cyber, bio, autonomy, agentic CTF) UK AISI runs against frontier models pre-release.
candidates.why_distinct: Increasingly the toolchain frontier labs coordinate through for pre-deployment safety testing.

candidates.name: SafeAgentBench
candidates.description: Safety evaluation for embodied/physical-world agent behavior.
candidates.why_distinct: Embodied-safety angle, distinct from digital-agent safety benchmarks.

candidates.name: MLCommons AILuminate
candidates.description: First cross-industry (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google et al. participated) standardized chat-safety benchmark, 12 hazard categories, 24K+ prompts, public graded leaderboard.
candidates.why_distinct: Closest thing to an industry-consensus safety leaderboard, not a single academic group's proposal.

candidates.name: BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA)
candidates.description: 58,000+ ambiguous trinary-choice QA questions across 9 social categories testing reliance on stereotypical shortcuts.
candidates.why_distinct: Standard bias benchmark; now mostly folded into HELM Safety composites.

candidates.name: ToxiGen
candidates.description: 274K machine-generated toxic/benign statements re: 13 minority groups, implicit hate-speech detection.
candidates.why_distinct: Pre-2023 vintage, rarely cited in current frontier releases.

candidates.name: AIR-Bench 2024 (AI Safety)
candidates.description: Comprehensive safety benchmark across 4 risk categories/8 hazard types, evaluates compliance with CAIS/OpenAI/EU AI Act standards.
candidates.why_distinct: Regulatory-compliance framing distinct from HarmBench's attack-success framing.

candidates.name: Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH)
candidates.description: Canonical single/multi-needle retrieval smoke test; by 2026 considered a baseline sanity check rather than a discriminating benchmark on its own.
candidates.why_distinct: Named explicitly in the Evidently AI article; the original long-context probe most others were built to surpass.

candidates.name: Global-MMLU
candidates.description: 42-language MMLU, human+machine translated. Gemini 3.1 Pro cited at 93.2%.
candidates.why_distinct: Directly cited by a frontier lab (Gemini technical report) -- real relevance signal; the catalog has zero multilingual coverage.

candidates.name: FLORES-200
candidates.description: 200-language translation-quality benchmark, professional-translated parallel sentences; used in Gemini's own technical report.
candidates.why_distinct: Translation-specific, complements Belebele's reading-comprehension framing.

candidates.name: Vals Index
candidates.description: GDP-weighted composite index across finance/legal/tax/coding agentic tasks -- an independent enterprise-facing benchmark aggregator.
candidates.why_distinct: Cross-domain composite specifically aimed at enterprise buyers, distinct provenance from academic benchmarks.

candidates.name: Scale AI SEAL Leaderboards (incl. PRBench)
candidates.description: Private, expert-curated, pairwise-graded evals across coding/instruction-following/math/multilingual, datasets stay unpublished so they can't be gamed. Includes PRBench (Professional Reasoning Bench, incl. legal).
candidates.why_distinct: The "Scale SEAL" the user's Reddit list specifically named, and the closest thing to a private-eval provenance category in this whole landscape -- distinct from every other source here.

candidates.name: CodeContests
candidates.description: Competitive-programming dataset (Codeforces/AtCoder/CodeChef) used in AlphaCode evaluations, strict test-case validation.
candidates.why_distinct: The dataset AlphaCode itself was evaluated against.

candidates.name: RepoBench
candidates.description: Repository-level code completion/retrieval benchmark.
candidates.why_distinct: Named explicitly in the Evidently AI article.

candidates.name: BeIR
candidates.description: Retrieval benchmark suite, largely superseded/absorbed by MTEB's retrieval tasks.
candidates.why_distinct: Named explicitly in the Evidently AI article.

candidates.name: ALFRED / VirtualHome
candidates.description: Household task-execution benchmarks: ALFRED (vision-language navigation+manipulation), VirtualHome (symbolic program execution in simulated rooms).
candidates.why_distinct: Foundational (2018/2020) but still used in current embodied-agent extensions.

candidates.name: Stanford HELM (+ HELM-Lite / MedHELM / VHELM / HEIM / AIR-Bench)
candidates.description: Open framework spanning 16+ scenarios x 7 axes (accuracy, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency, calibration); wraps MMLU-Pro/GPQA/IFEval so mostly not new data, but has unique satellite suites (MedHELM clinical, VHELM vision, HEIM text-to-image, AIR-Bench safety).
candidates.why_distinct: A meta-framework, not a single benchmark -- its own composite score isn't directly comparable to the catalog's per-benchmark rows; its satellite suites (MedHELM, VHELM) are the actual candidates worth pulling.

candidates.name: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 (Hugging Face)
candidates.description: HF's updated community leaderboard using 6 harder benchmarks (IFEval, BBH, MATH-Hard, MuSR, GPQA, MMLU-Pro) -- replaced the saturated v1 covered elsewhere in this catalog.
candidates.why_distinct: A composite of benchmarks already individually tracked (or candidates above, e.g. MuSR) -- add the components, not a "v2 score."

candidates.name: BrowserGym / AgentLab
candidates.description: Evaluation environments/frameworks that unify WebArena, WorkArena, VisualWebArena, AssistantBench, MiniWoB, and other suites under one harness.
candidates.why_distinct: A framework, not a benchmark with its own score -- add its constituent benchmarks individually instead.
